items.title: Toshiko Akiyoshi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999
items.q: The first great pianist I had met actually in person was Oscar Peterson. That was in 1953 I believe.

ctx.x: So Teddy Wilson — now I think I had read that you had a chance encounter with Oscar Peterson?

Yes. The first great pianist I had met actually in person was Oscar Peterson. That was in 1953 I believe. That was the first time the American jazz group came to Japan for the Japanese audience. Before that a few groups came to Japan but they were for the USO © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

tour for the American troops. For example, Louis Armstrong was there one time, and the Gene Krupa Trio was there one time, and way before that, in 1950 I believe there was a dance band, Les Brown’s band with Bob Hope. But more than anything, I think ’51, I’m not quite sure, there is Oscar Pettiford the leader, and J.J. Johnson and Howard McGhee, they were also on the USO tour. items.q: my first recording, which was done by Norman Granz, you know, at the recommendation from the late Oscar Peterson... we recorded from midnight, 'I'll give you Oscar's rhythm section,' which was that ... and of course Oscar didn't have drummer, so JATP—in Oscar's trio there wasn't any drummer—so JATP

ctx.x: And Bud Powell‟s record was … the first one, I think he was 23 years old, his first [as a] leader. And my first recording, which was done by Norman Granz, you know, at the recommendation from the late Oscar Peterson, I was 23 years old, so I thought, “Whoa, this is something!” [laughs]
